newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART REACH GERMAN CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART REACH GERMAN CUP FINAL.

text.p: Stuttgart booked their berth in the German Cup final on Wednesday night with a tight 2-1 victory over Hamburg.
A 60th minute goal by defender Thomas Schneider proved the difference between the two sides in this hard-fought battle.
Stuttgart, third in the German first division, now meet east German regional league side Cottbus Energie in the June 14 final at Berlin's Olympic Stadium.
The third division side became only the second regional league club in history to reach the final -- emulating Hertha Berlin's 1993 effort -- by beating Karlsruhe 3-0 on Tuesday.
Stuttgart's victory keeps alive their hopes of a league and cup double. They stand six points behind leaders Bayern Munich with seven games to go.

Bulgarian international Krassimir Balakow opened the scoring for Stuttgart after 15 minutes but former Stuttgart ace Juergen Hartmann levelled four minutes later and it took Schneider's effort on the hour to separate the teams.

"We just won by the skin of our teeth. We were lucky. Now we're pleased to be meeting Cottbus in the final. We've played them before... they are very good players," said Stuttgart's German international Fredi Bobic.
